simple.meaning: פַּרְעֹשׁ (parʻôsh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a flea (as the isolated insect).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2 times across 1 Samuel, beginning at 1 Samuel 24:15. Its contexts include blood, kingship, mountain, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פַּרְעֹשׁ (H6550).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

occurrences.englishText: May Yahweh therefore be judge, and give sentence between me and you, and see, and plead my cause, and deliver me out of your hand.”
Now therefore, don’t let my blood fall to the earth away from the presence of Yahweh; for the king of Israel has come out to seek a flea, as when one hunts a partridge in the mountains.”
